title: Compile first Manhattan road-tile fixture
acceptance: a roughly 20–30 block Manhattan fixture is compiled from real source geometry into deterministic 256 m logical tiles rather than hand-authored roads
generated tiles preserve one-to-one meter distances, roadbed/intersection shape, direction/lane metadata where source data supports it, and stable IDs across tile seams
the fixture includes a city/tile manifest and enough visual/collision geometry and metadata for a browser runtime to load without GIS libraries
seam tests demonstrate that roads crossing adjacent tile boundaries do not create visible or collision gaps in the fixture
the fixture is small and redistributable enough to support automated/runtime development or is generated deterministically from documented small inputs
verify: python3 -m pytest tools/map_compiler/tests -k 'tile or seam or fixture'
verification: PR #3 merged into main as c29796bee180997ec814b2f21f2af62b584a40a4. The official Flatiron/Madison Square snapshot contains 110 roadbed polygons and 71 CSCL centerline segments and deterministically compiles to 15 256 m tiles. T004 tile/seam/fixture tests, the full map-compiler suite, web runtime, project health, lint/schema, and Ubuntu Roach coordination checks passed on clean GitHub-hosted runners.

evidence.work: Official bounded NYC source snapshot, CSCL semantics adapter, deterministic 256 m tile compiler, 15 checked-in runtime tiles, manifest, and seam/determinism tests merged via PR #3
